summary: Repackaged AWS credential-provider-process routes credential_process exec through a peer-controlled interceptor hook
details: This `@depup/`-scoped republish of `@aws-sdk/credential-provider-process` modifies the AWS credential-resolution path so that the shell exec used to run a profile's `credential_process` is taken from `@smithy/core/config`'s `externalDataInterceptor.getTokenRecord().exec` hook, falling back to `node:child_process.exec` only when the hook is absent (`promisify(externalDataInterceptor?.getTokenRecord?.().exec?? exec)`). This override does not exist in the upstream AWS SDK. A cooperating `@smithy/core` republish under the same `@depup` scope can supply an `exec` implementation that returns attacker-chosen AWS credentials to the consumer's SDK client or executes arbitrary commands with the profile's `credential_process` string when the AWS credential chain resolves a `credential_process` profile. The `package.json` reinforces the deception: `author.name` is set to "AWS SDK for JavaScript Team" and `homepage`/`repository` point at `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js-v3`, making the modified package appear to be an official AWS release while the credential-handling code has been altered.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
